title: Commentary on the Sutra of Praise for the Pure Land Buddha’s Reception of Beings
author: Zhanran (commentary)
excerpt: The Amitabha Sutra is the essential teaching that the World-Honored One proclaimed without being asked, the profound sutra praised by the Buddhas of the ten directions, the wondrous Dharma of ultimate expedience, the consummate goal of perfect and sudden instruction. It is the most important scripture of the Pure Land school, called the First Sutra of the Pure Land, for in it Sakyamuni Buddha praises the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and reveals the certainty of rebirth in that land.

Textbook
Translated by imperial command by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang

The Amitabha Sutra is the essential teaching that the World-Honored One proclaimed without being asked, the profound sutra praised by the Buddhas of the ten directions, the wondrous Dharma of ultimate expedience, the consummate goal of perfect and sudden instruction. It is the most important scripture of the Pure Land school, called the First Sutra of the Pure Land, for in it Sakyamuni Buddha praises the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and reveals
the certain rebirth
in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss through
the path of liberation in this very life

. This path is praised with one voice by the Buddhas of the ten directions (including, of course, Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss). Those who deeply give rise to faith and understanding will surely be received and protected by the Buddhas of the ten directions (including, of course, Amitabha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss); those who practice as instructed will surely be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. The sutra says:
(The Buddhas of the ten directions)
each manifest the broad and long tongue, spreading it over the three-thousand great-thousand world, and, circling it all around, speak words of truth: ‘You sentient beings,
should all faithfully accept
this teaching of ‘praise of the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land, the Dharma-gate received by all Buddhas,’
The Dharma-gate
It is also said:
“If a good man or good woman, whether already having heard, or about to hear, or now hearing, has heard this sutra and deeply gives rise to faith and understanding.
Having given rise to faith and understanding,
they will surely be
received by such Tathagatas dwelling in the ten directions, [in number like] the sands of ten Ganges
(Ganges)
-rivers of Buddhas and World-Honored Ones,
received and protected
Those who practice as taught
, all of them
will surely
attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, never regressing; all of them
will surely be reborn
in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus.”

[The path of liberation in this very life] is the path by which, in this very life, one ends birth-and-death and escapes the three realms. Through the ordinary paths of practice, to end birth-and-death and escape the three realms one must completely eradicate afflictions; this is extremely difficult and all but impossible to reach within this very life. And if in this life one cannot end birth-and-death and escape the three realms, then, because of the delusion of passing from one birth to the next, no one knows in which life and in which kalpa one will again set foot upon the bodhi path. Yet the Buddha-recitation path that the World-Honored One reveals here needs only a mind held fast without confusion; at the moment of death one is certainly reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, thereby ending birth-and-death and escaping the three realms. This is something anyone can attain within this very life, so long as the method is correct and one strives with sincere and unremitting effort. Hence it is called the path of liberation in this very life, praised with one voice by the Buddhas of the ten directions. Those who deeply give rise to faith and understanding are surely received and protected by the Buddhas of the ten directions; those who practice as taught are surely reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. [The delusion of passing from one birth to the next] means forgetting everything at rebirth.

The Amitabha Sutra exists in two translations. One is the Sutra of the Buddha Speaks of Amitabha, translated by the great master Kumarajiva during the Yao Qin period, commonly called the Qin translation; the other is the Sutra of Praise for the Pure Land Buddha’s Reception of Beings, translated by the great master Xuanzang in the Tang dynasty, commonly called the Tang translation.

Responding to the Chinese people’s preference for concision, Master Kumarajiva translated chiefly by meaning: the text is brief yet rich in import, subtle and fluent. Master Xuanzang, in order to preserve the original appearance, translated word for word: accurate and complete, the original expressions retained, the wording clear and detailed, free of the faults of misunderstanding and invention, which is of vital importance for study and practice. When one studies the meaning of the sutra closely and sets the two translations side by side, one can reach a deeper and more accurate understanding.
For example, in the Sutra of the Buddha Speaks of Amitabha:

“Sariputra, if a good man or good woman hears this Amitabha Buddha and holds fast to his name, for one day, or two days, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven days, with a single mind without confusion, then at the end of life that person, with Amitabha Buddha and the holy assembly now appearing before him, will have a mind not inverted; at death he will be reborn in the supremely blissful land of Amitabha Buddha.”
In this passage there are two questions of deep concern to students of the Pure Land:
First, what is “a single mind without confusion”? For a long time there have been many conflicting views and endless debate.

Second, regarding the phrase “at the end of life, with a mind not inverted,” people often ask: in order to be reborn freely, must one, besides reaching a single mind without confusion, also avoid an inverted mind at the moment the four great elements dissolve at death?
The Sutra of Praise for the Pure Land Buddha’s Reception of Beings translates it thus:

“Sariputra, the pure-hearted good man or good woman who hears the name of Amitayus, the Tathagata, with its immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable merits, and the adorned merits of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and, having heard, reflects upon them; for one day or night, or two or three, or four or five, or six or seven, holds the mind without confusion. When that good man or good woman comes to the end of life, Amitayus Buddha, together with his countless sravaka disciples and the bodhisattvas, gathers before him, surrounding him front and back, and with compassionate protection causes his mind to be undisturbed. Having already abandoned life, he follows the Buddha’s assembly and is born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus.”
Setting the two side by side, it becomes clear:
First, “a single mind without confusion” is “held a mind without confusion.”

Second, “at the end of life, with a mind not inverted” is joined to the preceding phrase “Amitabha Buddha and the holy assembly now appearing before him,” meaning: Amitabha Buddha and the holy assembly appear before him and, with compassionate protection, cause his mind not to be inverted. That is to say, so long as one induces Amitabha Buddha to appear and receive one, even when the four great elements dissolve and the suffering presses in and maras appear, because of Amitabha Buddha’s compassionate protection, one’s mind will not be inverted.

A special word should be said: the Heart Sutra translated by Master Xuanzang is universally loved and known in every household, reaching everywhere without limit. The Sutra of Praise for the Pure Land Buddha’s Reception of Beings that he translated is also rendered with consummate skill—not only accurate and complete, its meaning detailed and its reasoning lucid, its literary polish brilliant, but it reads smoothly and trippingly on the tongue, attaining the highest realm of the translator’s art—faithfulness, fluency, and elegance—and possessing an extraordinarily powerful power to draw and hold the reader.

[Faithfulness, fluency, and elegance] For a translated work, to be wholly faithful to the original, accurate and complete, is called “faithfulness”; to be fluent in wording, “fluency”; to be brilliant in literary polish, “elegance.”
[The Sutra of Praise for the Pure Land Buddha’s Reception of Beings]

the title, ‘Praise of the Pure Land Buddha’s Reception of Beings,’ means that this sutra praises the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, and is the Dharma-gate received and protected by the Buddhas of the ten directions. In the sutra the Buddha says:

“Sariputra, for what reason is this sutra named ‘praise of the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land, the Dharma-gate received by all Buddhas’? Sariputra, because in this sutra the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus, and the Buddhas and World-Honored Ones of the ten directions, desiring by expeditious means to benefit and bring peace and joy to all sentient beings, each, abiding in his own land, display great miraculous transformations and speak words of truth, urging all sentient beings to faithfully accept this teaching. Therefore this sutra is named
‘praise of the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land, the Dharma-gate received by all Buddhas.’”

In this sutra, Sakyamuni Buddha praises the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss: the adornment of its environment, the adornment of its inhabitants; the absence of all suffering and the enjoyment of every happiness; immeasurable lifespan; meeting with hosts of all the highest good; and, never regressing, going on to Buddhahood. He likewise teaches the practice-path received by all Buddhas: holding the mind without confusion, and so being reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and passing beyond birth-and-death horizontally. In the sutra the Buddha says:

“The pure-hearted good man or good woman who hears the name of Amitayus, the Tathagata, with its immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable merits, and the adorned merits of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and, having heard, reflects upon them; for one day or night, or two or three, or four or five, or six or seven, holds the mind without confusion. When that good man or good woman comes to the end of life, Amitayus Buddha, together with his countless sravaka disciples and the bodhisattvas, gathers before him, surrounding him front and back, and with compassionate protection causes his mind to be undisturbed. Having already abandoned life, he follows the Buddha’s assembly and is born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus.”
The essential teaching of this sutra:
with faith and acceptance, make vows, practice as instructed, hold the mind without confusion, and be born in that Buddha-land.
In the sutra the World-Honored One says:

“The pure-hearted good man or good woman who hears the name of Amitayus, the Tathagata, with its immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable merits, and the adorned merits of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and, having heard, reflects upon them; for one day or night, or two or three, or four or five, or six or seven,
holds the mind without confusion

. When that good man or good woman comes to the end of life, Amitayus Buddha, together with his countless sravaka disciples and the bodhisattvas, gathers before him, surrounding him front and back, and with compassionate protection causes his mind to be undisturbed. Having already abandoned life, he follows the Buddha’s assembly and is born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus.”
Then, immediately, the World-Honored One adds:

“I observe this great causal occasion of such benefit and peace, and speak true words: the pure-hearted good man or good woman who hears the name of Amitayus, the Tathagata, with its inconceivable merits, and the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, should all
with faith and acceptance make the vow to practice as instructed and be born in that Buddha-land.
Therefore, “
practice as instructed
” means:

“The pure-hearted good man or good woman who hears the name of Amitayus, the Tathagata, with its immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable merits, and the adorned merits of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and, having heard, reflects upon them; for one day or night, or two or three, or four or five, or six or seven,
holds the mind without confusion
The sutra also says:
(The Buddhas of the ten directions)
each manifest the broad and long tongue, spreading it over the three-thousand great-thousand world, and, circling it all around, speak words of truth: ‘You sentient beings, you should all
faithfully accept
this teaching of ‘praise of the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land, the Dharma-gate received by all Buddhas.’”
The Dharma-gate
It is also said:
“You sentient beings should all
accept with faith and grasp the meaning
of the words of me and the Buddhas and World-Honored Ones of the ten directions, and diligently and earnestly
practice as instructed
, harboring no doubt.”

“For what reason is this sutra named ‘praise of the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land, the Dharma-gate received by all Buddhas’? Sariputra, because in this sutra the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus, and the Buddhas and World-Honored Ones of the ten directions, desiring by expeditious means to benefit and bring peace and joy to all sentient beings, each, abiding in his own land, display great miraculous transformations and speak words of truth, urging all sentient beings
faithfully to accept
this teaching. Therefore this sutra is named ‘praise of the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land, the Dharma-gate received by all
Buddhas
“If a good man or good woman, whether already having heard, or about to hear, or now hearing, has heard this sutra
and deeply gives rise to faith and understanding

, then, having given rise to faith and understanding, he will surely be received by such Tathagatas dwelling in the ten directions, [in number like] the sands of ten Ganges-rivers of Buddhas and World-Honored Ones. Those who practice as instructed will all surely attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, never regressing, and all surely be reborn in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus. Therefore, Sariputra. You sentient beings should all
accept with faith and grasp the meaning
of the words of me and the Buddhas of the ten directions, and diligently and earnestly
practice as instructed
, harboring no doubt.”
“Moreover, Sariputra. If a good man or good woman, regarding the adorned merits of the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus,
has made a vow, or, or will make a vow, or now makes a vow
, he will surely be received by such Tathagatas dwelling in the ten directions, [in number like] the sands of ten Ganges-rivers of Buddhas and World-Honored Ones.
Those who practice as instructed
will all surely attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, never regressing, and
all surely be reborn in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus
. Therefore, Sariputra, if there are pure-hearted good men or good women, they should all, regarding the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus,
deeply believe and, resolving with a sincere heart, vow to be reborn there, not giving way to indolence
“Moreover, Sariputra. In this defiled, enduring world of the five turbid and evil times, the pure-hearted good man or good woman who hears this teaching so hard to believe in all the world,
and can give rise to faith and understanding, accept, uphold, proclaim, and practice it as taught
, should be known as one most rare, who in immeasurable Buddha-fields has planted good roots. When such a person ends life,
he is surely reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss

, where he enjoys the various Mahayana joys of the adorned, pure Buddha-land. At every one of the six periods of day and night he draws near and makes offerings to Amitayus Buddha, ranges through the ten directions to make offerings to all Buddhas, and at the abodes of all Buddhas hears the Dharma and receives the prophecy. The stores of merit and wisdom swiftly reach fulfillment, and he quickly realizes the supreme, right, perfect enlightenment.”
with faith and acceptance, make vows, practice as instructed, hold the mind without confusion, and be born in that Buddha-land
”—in this sixteen-character essential teaching, “
practice as instructed
” links what has gone before and what comes after, and is the most crucial. Therefore the World-Honored One, time and again, over and over, in the sutra, earnestly charges us with it.
In the sutra the World-Honored One teaches:
“You sentient beings should all faithfully accept this teaching of ‘praise of the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land, the Dharma-gate received by all
Buddhas
Therefore,
Buddha-recitation to seek rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss is
the Dharma-gate received by all Buddhas, and the World-Honored One in this sutra concretely and clearly teaches how to cultivate this Dharma-gate.
After the World-Honored One has spoken of

“hearing the name of Amitayus, the Tathagata, with its immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable merits, and the adorned merits of the Land of Ultimate Bliss; reflecting upon them, for one day or night, or two or three, or four or five, or six or seven,
holding the mind without confusion

. When that good man or good woman comes to the end of life, Amitayus Buddha, together with his countless sravaka disciples and the bodhisattvas, gathers before him, surrounding him front and back, and with compassionate protection causes his mind to be undisturbed. Having already abandoned life, he follows the Buddha’s assembly and is born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus,”
he at once adds:
“The pure-hearted good man or good woman who hears the name of Amitayus, the Tathagata, with its inconceivable merits, and the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, should all
with faith and acceptance make the vow and practice as instructed
, and be born in that Buddha-land

Here the Buddha sets out faith, vows, and practice with complete clarity: faith is “faithfully accepting” the World-Honored One’s teaching above; the vow is making the vow “to practice as instructed and be born in that Buddha-land”; practice is practicing as instructed, holding the mind without confusion.

While faith and vows remain only in the head, they are merely a notion. Faith and vows must be practiced and carried out; only then are they genuine faith and sincere vows. Therefore genuine faith and sincere vows necessarily lead to vigorous practice. Without truly diligent cultivation, how can one verify what one believes? How can one fulfill what one has vowed? Faith and vows without practice are nothing but empty faith and idle vows.
In this sutra, the World-Honored One, over and over, time and again, stresses the need to “
practice as instructed

,” and clearly teaches: so long as one practices as instructed, one is received by the Buddhas of the ten directions, is surely reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, never regresses, and quickly attains the Buddha-fruit. His concern overflows in his words; the World-Honored One teaches:

“The pure-hearted good man or good woman who hears the name of Amitayus, the Tathagata, with its inconceivable merits, and the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, should all with faith and acceptance make the vow,
practice as instructed
, and be born in that Buddha-land.”
Those who practice as instructed

will all surely attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, never regressing, and all surely be reborn in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus. Therefore, Sariputra. You sentient beings should all
accept with faith and grasp the meaning of the words of me and the Buddhas of the ten directions
, and diligently and earnestly
practice as instructed
, harboring no doubt.”
Those who practice as instructed

will all surely attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, never regressing, and all surely be reborn in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus. Therefore, Sariputra. If there are pure-hearted good men or good women, they should all, regarding the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Amitayus, deeply believe and, resolving with a sincere heart, vow to be reborn there,
not giving way to indolence

“In this defiled, enduring world of the five turbid and evil times, the pure-hearted good man or good woman who hears this teaching so hard to believe in all the world, and can give rise to faith and understanding, accept, uphold, proclaim, and
practice it as taught

, should be known as one most rare, who in immeasurable Buddha-fields has planted good roots. When such a person ends life, he is surely reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, where he enjoys the various Mahayana joys of the adorned, pure Buddha-land.”
Therefore the student must deeply believe and grasp the meaning of “
practice as instructed
” and put it into action, zealous day after day, pressing forward without pause.
[Zealous] Diligent and untiring.

The most striking feature of this sutra is: praised by the Buddhas of the ten directions, received by all Buddhas, passing beyond birth-and-death horizontally, never regressing, and attaining Buddhahood in a single lifetime.
[Praised by the Buddhas of the ten directions]:
The sutra says:
(The Buddhas of the ten directions)

each manifest the broad and long tongue, spreading it over the three-thousand great-thousand world, and, circling it all around, speak words of truth: ‘You sentient beings, you should all faithfully accept this teaching of ‘praise of the merits of the inconceivable Buddha-land, the Dharma-gate received by all Buddhas.’”
[Received by all Buddhas]:
The sutra says:

“If a good man or good woman, whether already having heard, or about to hear, or now hearing, has heard this sutra and deeply gives rise to faith and understanding. Having given rise to faith and understanding, he will surely be received by such Tathagatas dwelling in the ten directions, [in number like] the sands of ten Ganges
(Ganges)
-rivers of Buddhas and World-Honored Ones.”
[Passing beyond birth-and-death horizontally]
Master Yinguang says:

“Why is Buddha-recitation, seeking rebirth in the West, called the horizontally-transcending path? The ancients had a simile to explain it: they liken an ordinary being replete with delusion and karma to a worm born in the lowest joint of a bamboo, and this bamboo to the three realms. The worm wants to get out by only two means: one is to bore straight up, the other to bore straight across. To bore straight up means, from the lowest stage, to gnaw through joint after joint, and only when the topmost joint is pierced can it come out. This likens
(the simile)
cultivating other paths, which require eradicating all the views and thought afflictions before one can emerge from the three realms
(only then can one escape the three realms and end birth-and-death)

. The view delusions number eighty-eight, the thought delusions eighty-one grades; these many grades are likened to the joints of a bamboo. The worm boring straight up is called the vertical emergence. For example, a sage of the first fruit who has cut off the view delusions must pass through seven births in heaven and seven births among humans, through long kalpas of cultivation, before he can realize arhatship and end birth-and-death. One of the second fruit must likewise pass once through heaven and once among humans before realizing the fourth fruit. One of the third fruit, having already exhausted the thought delusions of the desire realm, must still, in the five no-return heavens, gradually cultivate before he can exhaust the thought delusions and realize the fourth fruit. Only then is he a non-learner sage who has left the three realms. If one of the third fruit is of dull faculties, he must further be born in the four formless heavens, from the heaven of the sphere of infinite space up to the heaven of neither perception nor non-perception, before he can realize the fourth fruit. This vertical path is thus arduous and long-drawn-out. To bore straight across is for this worm, instead of boring through joint by joint, simply to gnaw a hole straight sideways and so come out. Such a method is far easier than the vertical one. Those who recite the Buddha’s name are likewise. Though they have not eradicated the views and thought afflictions
(the views and thought delusions)

, yet if they can be complete in the three provisions of the Pure Land—faith, vows, and practice—then at death they can influence Amitabha Buddha to come and receive them, to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Once in that pure land, the views and thought afflictions are cut off of themselves. Why? Because the land’s environment is supreme and its conditions are strong, so there are no conditions that stir up afflictions in people. Thus one attains the three non-regressions, until he has broken through the dust-mote-like
(dust-mote delusions)
ignorance
(ignorance delusions)
, and realizes supreme bodhi
(Buddhahood)

—how direct and easy a matter! Hence the ancients say, studying the Way through other paths is like an ant climbing a high mountain; Buddha-recitation and rebirth in the West is like a sailboat riding the current.”
(From Talks on Returning to Lingyan from Shanghai)

[The three realms] The desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm. The desire realm is the world where beings possessed of the two desires of sex and food dwell, including above the six heavens of desire, in the middle humans and animals, and below the hungry ghosts and hells. The form realm is the world of beings who, without the two desires of sex and food, still have a body of form, including the eighteen heavens of the four meditations. The formless realm is the world of beings who have no body of form but abide in mind-consciousness in deep meditative concentration, including the four heavens of formlessness (the heaven of infinite space, the heaven of infinite consciousness, the heaven of nothingness, and the heaven of neither perception nor non-perception). These three realms are all the round of birth-and-death for ordinary beings, so the first aim of the Buddhist practitioner is to escape the three realms.
[The three non-regressions]

First, non-regression of stage, the stage one has attained is not lost; second, non-regression of practice, one does not fall away from the practice one has undertaken; third, non-regression of mindfulness, one does not turn back from right mindfulness. [The views and thought delusions] The view delusions and the thought delusions. The view delusions are the deluded errors of ordinary beings in their views, such as the view of self, the view of extremes, the perverse view, the view of attachments, and the view of moral prohibitions and precepts, the five wrong views. The thought delusions are the deluded errors of ordinary beings in their thoughts, such as greed, anger, delusion, pride, and doubt. These two delusions are the root cause of sentient beings wandering in the three realms to undergo birth-and-death fruitlessly; cutting them off enables one to end birth-and-death and escape the three realms. [The dust-mote delusions] The dust-mote delusions are the delusions of bodhisattvas. If a bodhisattva, in saving sentient beings, has not mastered the countless Dharma-gates like dust and sand, he cannot complete the work of teaching sentient beings; hence they are called the dust-mote delusions. [The ignorance delusions] The ignorance delusion is the fundamental ignorance that can obscure the principle of the ultimate reality of the Middle Way; cut it off completely and one becomes a Buddha.
[Never regressing]
The sutra says:
“All beings born in that land never regress.”
[Attaining Buddhahood in a single lifetime]
The sutra says:
“All beings born in that land never regress, and will never fall again into the evil destinies, border regions, lowly outcast
(lowly castes)
among them; they constantly roam the pure Buddha-lands of all Buddhas, and their supreme practices and vows advance with every thought, and they are certain to realize anuttara-samyak-sambodhi
(Buddhahood)
[Translated by imperial command by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang]

[Tripitaka Master] “Tripitaka” means the sutra-pitaka, the vinaya-pitaka, and the abhidharma-pitaka. The sutra-pitaka consists of the scriptures spoken by the Buddha; the vinaya-pitaka, of the precepts laid down by the Buddha; the abhidharma-pitaka, of the treatises composed by the Buddha’s disciples. A “Tripitaka Master” is a monk who is thoroughly versed in all three pitakas. [Xuanzang] Master Xuanzang (

), a celebrated Tripitaka Master of the Tang dynasty, is ranked with Kumarajiva and Paramartha as one of the three great translators of Chinese Buddhism, and was one of the founders of the Consciousness-only school. [Translated by imperial command] Master Xuanzang translated this sutra by order of Emperor Taizong of the Tang.

Master Xuanzang was born in the second year of the Renshou era of the Sui dynasty. As a child he followed his elder brother, the Dharma Master Changjie, to live at Jidu Monastery [sic] in Luoyang, where he studied Buddhism. At eleven (
) he already read fluently the Lotus Sutra and the Vimalakirti Sutra. At thirteen (

), when Luoyang held the examination for ordaining monks, though still young, he was chosen out of the ordinary because of his outstanding examination results. Afterwards he heard the Dharma Master Jing lecture on the Nirvana Sutra, learned the Compendium from the Dharma Master Yan, and, ascending the seat to repeat the teaching, analyzed it in detail, winning the admiration of the assembly.

[The examination for ordaining monks] In ancient times, the court established a system of ordaining monks to control the number of monks and nuns, to ensure their quality, and to forbid private ordination. It was stipulated that anyone seeking to leave home must pass an examination on the Buddhist scriptures before being permitted to shave and be ordained.

Later, Master Xuanzang traveled to various places to study, and soon exhausted the doctrines of every school; his ability was highly praised and his fame filled the capital. The President of the Department of State Affairs, Xiao Yu, memorialized the throne asking that he be settled at Zhuangyan Monastery. Because he felt deeply that the various teachings he had heard over many years in different places were inconsistent, and especially that the two schools current at the time, the She-lun school (later absorbed into the Dharma-character school) and the Di-lun school, disagreed greatly on the characteristics of phenomena, he longed for the Yogacarabhumi Sastra, which gathers together the teachings of the three vehicles, in order to fuse and unify all of it, and so resolved to go to India to seek the Dharma.
Because he could not obtain the travel permit (passport) issued by the Tang court, he never fulfilled his wish. In

years old), Master Xuanzang determinedly set out on his own from Chang’an, risking the journey to Tianzhu (present-day India). Under extraordinarily dangerous and arduous conditions, with an unyielding heroic spirit, he overcame countless difficulties and perils and finally reached Tianzhu.

During his more than ten years in Tianzhu, Master Xuanzang attended and consulted many famous eminent monks. Among the monasteries where he stayed was the great center of Buddhist learning of that era, Nalanda Monastery. He studied the Yogacarabhumi Sastra and the other sutras and treatises under that monastery’s abbot, the great Indian Buddhist authority, the Dharma Master Silabhadra. Silabhadra was a disciple of Dharmapala and a grand-disciple of Vasubandhu. In the thirteenth year of the Zhenguan era, Master Xuanzang lectured on the Mahayanasamgraha and the Vijnaptimatrata-siddhi on behalf of the Dharma Master Silabhadra at Nalanda. Afterward, he also traveled on foot throughout the whole of the South Asian subcontinent.

Master Xuanzang was not only profoundly versed in the Buddha-Dharma but also skilled in Sanskrit, so he took part repeatedly in religious debate assemblies and won them all, his reputation rising daily. At the invitation of the King of Magadha, Harsha, he presided over the great open debate assembly at Kanyakubja, extolling the Mahayana teaching. Present were the kings of eighteen countries, more than three thousand monks of both the Greater and Lesser Vehicles, more than two thousand Brahmins and heterodox disputants, and over a thousand monks of Nalanda. The Master took the seat of the main disputant and addressed the assembly, declaring: “If there is in my words a single phrase without reason, and anyone can refute it, I beg that my head be cut off [in atonement].” He waited eighteen days, and in the end no one dared come forward to dispute, so he won without a battle. When the assembly dispersed, all were greatly delighted, exclaiming that such a thing had never been seen. Thus his fame rose like a thunderclap and shook all of Tianzhu. The Mahayanists called him Mahayana Deva (Deva of the Great Vehicle), the Hinayanists called him Moksa Deva (Deva of Liberation), and King Harsha bowed to him as his teacher.

, a memorial hall to Master Xuanzang was established in the monastery. The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda became an architectural memorial to Master Xuanzang’s westward journey in search of the Dharma and his translation of the scriptures upon his return.

With the vigorous support of Emperor Taizong, Master Xuanzang established a scripture-translation institute (a state translation bureau) in Chang’an, where outstanding scholars from all over the country and from East Asian lands took part in translation. He spent more than ten years, within the Yuhua Palace, rendering a great many scriptures into Chinese. These Buddhist scriptures were later transmitted from China to the Korean peninsula, Vietnam, and Japan.
